The relationship between the 135 cm sphere reported operating at SNOLAB since 2021 and the 135 cm sphere reported running a 10-day physics run at LSM in 2024 is not resolved by any source fetched this session; both are recorded as separate sourced facts rather than merged into one assumed narrative.

physics_goals.quote: The NEWS-G collaboration intends to achieve sub-GeV/c2 Weakly Interacting Massive Particles (WIMPs) detection using Spherical Proportional Counters (SPCs).
value: Detect sub-GeV/c^2 WIMPs via single-ionization-electron sensitivity in spherical proportional counters

summary.plain: NEWS-G hunts for very light dark matter particles using a large hollow copper ball filled with gas, deep underground. A small 60 cm version ran in France; a bigger 135 cm sphere has been running at SNOLAB in Canada since 2021.
summary.technical: Spherical proportional counter (SPC) dark matter search: the 60 cm SEDINE detector (Ne+CH4, 3.1 bar) at LSM set limits in 2015; the current 135 cm copper sphere ('S140', pure CH4 at 135 mbar) was installed at SNOLAB in 2020-2021 with first signals in summer 2021 and continues operating with methane, neon and helium fills as of a September 2025 paper. A 135 cm sphere also ran a 10-day methane physics run at LSM reported in July 2024.

unique_capabilities.quote: low capacitance, low energy threshold, excellent energy resolution, single readout channel (in its simplest version), low cost, robustness, and flexibility in gas choice and operating pressure
value: Spherical Proportional Counter: single readout channel, low capacitance, single-ionization-electron threshold, flexible gas choice (methane, neon, helium mixtures)
